intro.title: Write a custom map polyfill
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom version of JavaScript's built-in `map` method from scratch, called a polyfill. You'll learn how `map` works under the hood by creating a function that iterates over an array, applies a callback to each element, and returns a new array with the transformed results. The core concepts involved are array iteration, callback functions, and handling edge cases like empty arrays. This exercise will help you understand functional programming patterns and how to extend JavaScript's native capabilities.
intro.usecase: The map method is a foundational tool for data transformation in real-world applications. For instance, in an e-commerce dashboard, developers use map to convert raw product data into formatted display objects for a product grid. Similarly, in a form builder, map processes an array of field configurations to render interactive input components. Understanding how to implement a custom map polyfill deepens your grasp of functional programming patterns essential for building scalable, data-driven UIs.
